title: DVT and PE: acute, chronic or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic DVT.

HPI
The patient is a 36-year-old woman presenting for a routine follow-up regarding chronic deep vein thrombosis of the right femoral vein. She reports that she has been stable on her current anticoagulant regimen. She denies any current swelling, pain, or shortness of breath. She notes that she has been able to maintain her activity level without complications.

Medication List
Apixaban 5 mg twice daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination of the right lower extremity shows no signs of edema or erythema. Skin is intact with no warmth or tenderness noted over the right femoral vein. Pulse is palpable.

Assessment
1. Chronic deep vein thrombosis of the right femoral vein. Ultrasound confirms the presence of a residual clot.

Plan
The patient will continue her current long-term anticoagulation therapy. She was instructed to monitor for any signs of calf pain or swelling and to report any concerns immediately. Follow-up is scheduled in six months.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Chronic DVT of the right femoral vein: I82.511 (HCC 267).

distractors.why: The DVT is documented as chronic.
Chronic DVT is a current condition, not history.
